fullPassage: One of the main obstacles in anyone's quest for longevity is the fact that the skills that my colleagues and I acquired during our medical training have proved to be far more effective against fast death than slow death. We learned to fix broken bones, wipe out infections with powerful antibiotics, support and even replace damaged organs, and decompress serious spine or brain injuries. We had an amazing ability to save lives and restore full function to broken bodies, even reviving patients who were nearly dead. But we were markedly less successful at helping our patients with chronic conditions, such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, or neurological disease, evade slow death. We could relieve their symptoms and often delay the end slightly, but it didn't seem as if we could reset the clock the way we could with acute problems. We had become better at catching the eggs, but we had little ability to stop them from falling off the building in the first place.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

One of the main obstacles in anyone's quest for longevity is the fact ① that the skills ② that my colleagues and I acquired during our medical training ③ have proved ④ being far more effective against fast death than slow death.

det.korean: prove + to부정사: 'proved to be'. being → to be
det.analysis:
✅ ④ being → to be: prove to be = ~임이 밝혀지다
❌ ① that: 명사절 접속사, 적절
❌ ② that: 관계대명사(주격), 적절
❌ ③ have proved: 현재완료, 적절
det.tip: prove to be + 형용사/명사: ~임이 입증되다

det.korean: 전치사 at 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. help → helping
det.analysis:
✅ ④ help → helping: at + 동명사. 'be successful at helping'
❌ ① to save: ability to + 동사원형, 적절
❌ ② reviving: 분사구문, 적절
❌ ③ less successful: 비교급, 적절

❌ ② such as: 예시 도입, 적절
❌ ④ delay: and 병렬(relieve and delay), 적절

✅ ③ 3번 뒤: '시계 리셋 불가' → 달걀 비유로 한계 요약
❌ ① 너무 이른 위치
❌ ② 급성 치료 능력 설명 중간에 결론 삽입 어색
❌ ④ 만성 질환 언급 후 곧바로 달걀 비유는 가능하나, 시계 리셋 비유 뒤가 더 자연스러움

❌ ③ (C)-(B): 결론 먼저는 논리 역전

det.tip: 논리 흐름: 능력 제시 → 한계 발견 → 비유로 결론

questions.passage: One of the main obstacles in anyone's quest for longevity is the fact that the skills that my colleagues and I acquired during our medical training have proved to be far more effective against fast death than slow death. We learned to fix broken bones, wipe out infections with powerful antibiotics, support and even replace damaged organs, and decompress serious spine or brain injuries. We had an amazing ability to save lives and restore full function to broken bodies, even reviving patients who were nearly dead. But we were markedly less successful at helping our patients with chronic conditions, such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, or neurological disease, evade slow death. We could relieve their symptoms and often delay the end slightly, but it didn't seem as if we could reset the clock the way we could with acute problems. We had become better at catching the eggs, but we had little ability to stop them from falling off the building in the first place.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 급성 문제에 비해 만성 질환 치료가 얼마나 덜 성공적이었는지를 나타내는 부사를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: 'we were markedly less successful' — 현저하게 덜 성공적이었다.
det.analysis: markedly — 현저하게. marked → markedly(부사)
det.tip: markedly = noticeably = significantly = 현저하게
